Header: Busseola fusca, Eldana saccharina , Chilo partellus

Prevention: Stem borers are difficult to control once in a field.
It is worthwhile therefore putting in effort to prevent them
Collect and burn any infected stems and crop residues to kill hibernating life stages
Plant early at the beginning of the rains
Clear volunteer sorghum crop that could harbour the pest
Destroy alternative hosts especially in and around the sorghum fields before it heads
Rotate sorghum with non-host plants especially non-cereals (beans, cassava, sweet potato, soybean etc).
Maintain a legume (cowpea, desmodium)/ sorghum intercrop to reduce incidence of stem borers
Monitoring: Start looking for signs of damage when plants are 2 to 4 weeks old, depending on the area.
If you find damage (holes in the leaves) then constitute a control program
Look for a dead heart (drying of the youngest leaf) during the early stage of infestation
Direct Control: Mix dry clay or sawdust with small neem ( Azadirachta indica ) powder (ground neem seeds) at a rate of 1:1 and place in the funnel of the plant
Wood ash or soil, or a mixture of both can be used to control stem borers.
Sieve the ash or soil to remove any larger particles, which could damage the plant.
Take about a teaspoonful of the soil or ash and put it into the funnel made by the new leaves.
Do not use too much soil or ash as it can damage the leaves.
It is best to use the ash or soil before any sign of stem borer attack
Restrictions: Consult your extension worker and always read the label for direction on use
Always wear protective gear (overalls, gumboots, goggles, caps, gloves and face masks) when handling chemicals
